title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to test whether constrained prompting plus deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback (generate→verify→repair, one allowed repair) increases deterministic-verifier semantic-correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level device configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents, shared_initial_candidate execution semantics, model = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Each intent produced one initial generation shared across baseline and guarded conditions; the guarded pipeline could invoke at most one additional repair call. Results: baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.006667 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Only one guarded repair was applied (model_calls_used = 151 total). Interpretation: on this preregistered synthetic corpus the guarded workflow produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline. We report execution accounting, clarify runtime-sampling semantics (the archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset; no deterministic sampling or fixed seed was enforced), and emphasize the methodological lesson that baseline calibration is required to avoid ceiling effects that invalidate preregistered power assumptions. All execution artifacts and analysis files are archived in the recorded execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Natural-language intent interfaces promise to lower operator burden by letting humans express desired network changes as free-text intents that are automatically translated into executable device configurations. Prior work documents that single-pass LLM outputs frequently contain syntactic errors, omissions, or semantic violations that can produce unsafe or unavailable network states if applied directly [1],[2],[3]. In response, operational architectures commonly adopt a generate→verify→repair pattern: an LLM generates a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks intent-level invariants or formally derived invariants, and a repair loop or human gate corrects violations before execution [4],[5]. Security analyses further motivate deterministic gating because unchecked textual claims can be converted into harmful actions in multi-tool agentic workflows [6].

Research question and scope. After an autonomous literature review we preregistered the confirmatory question used here: does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase deterministic-verifier semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation compared with unconstrained baseline prompting under a paired design? The trial was preregistered and frozen prior to model interactions (preregistration id: study_cand_2026_b2_v1). We restrict claims to performance on the deterministic synthetic corpus and on verifier-level pass/fail outcomes; no production generalization is asserted.
sections.related_work:
Related literature covers three relevant strands. First, intent-to-configuration research documents the difficulty of converting operator free text to verifier-sound artifacts and reports modest semantic-correctness rates on public benchmarks, motivating post-generation checks and formalization efforts [1],[2]. Second, generate→verify→repair architectures—ranging from verifier-in-the-loop fine-tuning to policy-guided verifier feedback—have demonstrated improvements for infrastructure-as-code and configuration-repair tasks, but reported effect sizes vary with baseline model competence, repair budget, and sampling semantics [4],[7]. Third, security and systems analyses have demonstrated claim-to-action vulnerabilities where LLM outputs plus tool access produce harmful actions, reinforcing the need for auditable gating and verifier-aware planning in NetOps agentic pipelines [6],[8].

Positioning. Our trial operationalizes a narrowly specified guarded architecture and emphasizes preregistration, paired inference, and deterministic-verifier endpoints. Key contrasts with prior work that reports larger guarded-vs-baseline gains are: (a) shared_initial_candidate execution semantics (one initial sample shared across conditions), (b) a strict one-repair budget per intent, (c) a single tested model (gpt-5-mini), and (d) a synthetic verifier-capable task bank restricted to small topologies. These design choices bound the observable marginal benefit of one repair under the chosen estimand and explain why previously reported larger gains can coexist with our bounded result [4],[7].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study preregistration (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) defined a paired_binary design with primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and an exact two-sided McNemar test as the confirmatory inference. Key frozen constraints: N=150 confirmatory intents; exactly one initial model call per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics); at most one guarded repair call per intent. Inclusion/exclusion rules were preregistered (rule-based ambiguity detector, verifier-coverage checks), as were missingness handling (one deterministic retry on API timeout then mark failed) and multiplicity plans. The preregistered power plan targeted a 15-percentage-point absolute improvement (≈80% power) under conservative discordant-pair assumptions; that assumption is evaluated in Results.

Task generation and corpus. Confirmatory tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and cover four intent families: reachability/isolation, ACL-like access changes, VLAN/MTU sequence changes, and uplink switchover patterns. Topologies were constrained to verifier-capable small networks (4–32 nodes). Pre-execution mapping and verifier-coverage unit-tests were applied; no confirmatory exclusions occurred. Representative task manifests (archived) indicate a range of labeled difficulties (medium, hard, very_hard) and deterministic generator seeds that make the corpus reproducible.

Model, adapter, and deterministic validator. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (provider record: openai_responses). The execution adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) enforced the one-initial/≤one-repair budget per intent. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule and returned a boolean pass/fail, normalized final-configuration text, and diagnostics (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes).

Runtime-sampling semantics (explicit clarification requested by review). The archived execution model configuration records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset) in model_configuration.json. Null/unset does not imply deterministic temperature=0; no numeric temperature or fixed random seed was enforced. Therefore model outputs may be nondeterministic across independent API sessions. This literal recording is preserved in the archive and is reflected in the Disclosure Statement.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and inferential meaning (explicit statement requested by review). The execution contract implemented shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent exactly one initial model generation was produced and that identical sampled candidate was used to evaluate both baseline and guarded conditions. The guarded pipeline could invoke at most one additional repair call only if the deterministic verifier failed that initial candidate. Consequently, the baseline success rate measures the validity of the single initial sampled candidate; the guarded vs baseline contrast isolates the marginal effect of the single allowed repair applied to that identical candidate. This inference differs from independent-sampling designs (per-condition draws) whose estimands include sampling variability across draws.

Execution accounting, retries, and contamination controls. Planned episodes = 300 (150 tasks × 2 conditions); completed_episode_count = 300; complete_pair_count = 150. The adapter recorded model_calls_used = 151 (150 shared_initial generations + 1 repair call). Provider-call auditing reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 151, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 150, repair: 1}, and condition_counts = {shared: 150, guarded: 1}. Contamination checks reported zero flags. Missingness policy was not invoked because there were no API or parsing failures.
sections.results:
Execution and provider audit. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150. model_calls_used = 151 and artifact_hash_count = 1058 are recorded in the execution manifest. analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty (no contamination flags); mapping and verifier unit-tests passed prior to batch execution.

Primary numerical outcomes and contingency. The paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline) were: n_11 = 149 (both-pass), n_10 = 1 (guarded-only-pass), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-pass), n_00 = 0 (both-fail). Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points).

Statistical inference and uncertainty quantification. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test on the observed discordant counts produced p = 1.0 (two-sided exact), indicating no statistically significant difference under the preregistered test. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.02]. These numeric facts are direct extractions from analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/condition_summary.csv) and the archived analysis log.

Repair diagnostics and revision counts. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150), consistent with the near-ceiling initial correctness. That single repair converted one initially invalid candidate to a valid configuration under the deterministic validator. Median revision iterations for guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Validator traces for each episode provide validation_before and validation_after states, normalized_configuration strings, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, and valid flag; representative traces are archived (execution/scoring/task-00000X-*.json).

Representative examples. Representative task-000001: intent — "Migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600. For safety, shut edge1 down before changing either VLAN or MTU, then restore it to admin up." Shared-initial and both condition responses returned the expected four-command sequence; validator recorded parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, and valid = true (see execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json). Similar archived examples (tasks 000002–000006) show difficulty labels (medium→very_hard) and normalized configurations that demonstrate the generator produced nontrivial workflows while the tested model achieved near-ceiling correctness on the frozen corpus.

Sensitivity and preregistration assumptions. The preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats missing guarded outputs as failures was not needed because failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0 and unscorable episodes = 0. The principal mismatch with preregistration is empirical: the baseline success rate (≈99.33%) greatly exceeded the pilot assumption used for power planning (baseline ≈35% used to compute N). This produced a ceiling effect that removed headroom for demonstrating the targeted 15-percentage-point improvement and rendered the preregistered power calculation inapplicable to the observed data.
sections.discussion:
Methodological lessons: baseline calibration and sampling semantics. The primary scientific lesson concerns methodology for preregistered NetOps trials. Our preregistered power plan assumed a substantially lower baseline; observed baseline ≈99.33% leaves effectively no headroom for the guarded repair to produce large absolute gains. We therefore recommend a short baseline-calibration pilot (a few dozen tasks across the intended difficulty spectrum) to estimate baseline competence for the chosen model, prompt style, and generator difficulty prior to fixing N. Additionally, explicitly recording generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent per-condition sampling) is essential: they define distinct estimands and affect detectable marginal gains from repairs.

Operational interpretation beyond binary pass/fail. Deterministic guarded workflows yield operational artifacts not captured by binary verification: auditable normalized configurations, concise validator diagnostics (parsed_command_count, violation_codes) that accelerate human triage, and a standardized repair prompt for operator review. The presence of these operational affordances can be valuable even when marginal verifier-pass improvements are small on constrained corpora. Practitioners should weigh operational auditability and triage benefits alongside raw pass-rate deltas.

Threats to validity and limitations (artifact-grounded). Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics reduce sampling variance but do not capture per-condition sampling randomness; adapter-enforced call budgets and provider audit mitigate cross-condition leakage (cross_condition_cache_reuse_observed = false). Construct validity: deterministic validator pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; we mitigated mapping risk with unit-tests and archived mapping artifacts, but residual mis-evaluation risk remains. External validity: single-model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic corpus, and small topologies constrain production inference. Conclusion validity: preregistered power assumptions were violated by the unexpectedly high baseline; reported p-values and CIs correctly reflect observed counts but cannot overturn the ceiling limitation.

Recommendations for subsequent confirmatory designs. To address the remaining open questions identified by the literature synthesis (scaling, robustness, and adversarial resilience), future preregistered trials should (a) use baseline-calibration pilots to set N or difficulty, (b) explicitly choose generation semantics appropriate to the operational question (independent sampling if average-case across draws is of interest), (c) preregister multiple-repair budgets and repair strategies, and (d) broaden model diversity and topology scale while maintaining deterministic verifier coverage or adapting verifier invariants to larger topologies.

Reproducibility and artifact availability (compact guidance). All execution artifacts are archived in the execution bundle referenced by the execution manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, analysis/*). Key numeric facts in this paper are drawn directly from those artifacts: complete_pair_count = 150; baseline_success_count = 149; guarded_success_count = 150; model_calls_used = 151; paired contingency counts n_11 = 149, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0; exact McNemar p = 1.0; bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); users interested in runtime-sampling metadata can inspect that artifact. Representative scoring traces are available (execution/scoring/task-00000{1..6}-*.json) and substantiate the example workflows reported above.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting with constrained-template prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a deterministic synthetic corpus using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased the verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically tiny and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The principal scientific contribution is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials require baseline calibration and explicit generation-semantics specification to produce interpretable power calculations and estimands. Practically, our artifacts bound the marginal benefit of a one-repair guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics on this frozen synthetic corpus; evaluating independent-sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, multiple model families, and production-scale topologies remains necessary to answer broader operational questions.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
